card.problem: On weekly expiry afternoons, NIFTY tends to stay stuck near large open-interest strikes. Do short-horizon stretches away from the recent mean revert more on expiry days than on other days?
card.motivation: Ni, Pearson and Poteshman (JFE 2005) document pinning of underlyings to strikes at option expiry. Avellaneda and Lipkin (2003) model it as delta hedging by option holders who are long gamma. NIFTY weekly options carry very large open interest, so the hedging pressure on expiry afternoons should be big. This is the long-gamma counterpart to h1's short-gamma momentum card and uses a different signal (a zscore of price, not the return since the previous close), restricted to dte == 0.
card.approach: On expiry day after 13:00, fade 1m closes that sit more than k sigma from their 30-bar mean.
card.plan: Feature cz = zscore(close, 30) and dte. Entry only when dte == 0 and minute_of_day >= 225 (13:00). At most 3 trades per day, stop_atr 0.75 / take_atr 0.75 (atr_days 14), time exit 15:20. CPCV over zthr. A control run with the same rule on dte >= 2 days should show weaker results.
card.mechanism: Holders and writers who are net long gamma near the pinned strike sell into rises and buy into dips to stay delta-neutral, and gamma becomes very large as expiry nears. Directional intraday traders chasing the move pay the hedgers who supply this reversion.
card.rule: long: dte == 0 and minute_of_day >= 225 and cz < -p.zthr; short: dte == 0 and minute_of_day >= 225 and cz > p.zthr; exit stop/take 0.75 ATR or 15:20

zthr.source: A 2-sigma band, as in Gatev, Goetzmann and Rouwenhorst (RFS 2006). Grid [1.5, 2.0, 2.5].

kill: CPCV median path SR <= 0 after costs
the same rule on dte >= 2 days has an equal or higher SR, which would mean it is not expiry pinning
fewer than 100 trades in the research window, too thin to judge

replies.author: validator
replies.body:
h4 round 1: FAIL (gate a13f4a4b)
The report doesn't say whether this was the demo gate, so I'm not stating which thresholds applied. The gate stopped at the first real check, min_bets. The other checks were not run, so there are no PSR, DSR, PBO, costs or concentration numbers to explain.
- passed: probe (clean), determinism (identical).
- failed: min_bets, 40 bets vs ≥50. The strategy didn't trade enough for any statistic to mean anything. Net over those 40 bets is -4.6L. I wouldn't read that as a verdict on the idea, only that it is too thin to test.
- not run: everything after min_bets.
- patch: patch 1 of 4 was allowed, so it isn't a hard stop. What the report points at is trade count: the entry is only on expiry days, from 13:00, so the rule fires rarely. A one-rule patch could target how often it fires, argued from training folds only, and it would have to reach 50 bets. The report doesn't say which rule to change, and it doesn't show whether more trades would be profitable.

replies.author: coder
replies.body: h4 round 1: I'm not writing h4v2, and I recommend stopping h4. With only 40 bets, the card's own kill condition is hit: "fewer than 100 trades in the research window, too thin to judge". Widening the entry to get more trades would mean leaving expiry day or starting before 13:00, and either one drops the pinning mechanism the card tests.
